title: A MORPHOGRAPHIC IDEONOMIC ATLAS OF THE "INTUITIVELY SCALED OVERALL MUTUAL 'ANALOGOUSNESS'" OF "FORTY KEY GENERA OF FORMS"

lists.name: TABLE OF CONTENTS (The Forty 'Genera of Forms' Whose Mutual Analogical Proximities Are Treated In This Atlas)

notes: N=40. FORMS & Morphology. CAVEATS AND EXPLANATIONS: (1) The 'analogousness' values were MERELY DEDUCED (calculated indirectly) via the still uncertain but presumably somewhat <weak and defective> SCALE-SCALOR INVERSION METHOD, by the inversion of an earlier Triadic MDS Method table of DIRECTLY estimated 'analogousness' values of a set of merely 32 Form Genera (then serving as scalees) to a set of 40 Scaling Dyads containing 80 (40 x 2) antimonadic scalors (representing 40 Irredundant Genera). (2) However, both the LEFT and RIGHT SETS OF ANTIMONADS were used to produce the atlas, which means that each Form Genus has been scaled via 2 x 32 = 64 Virtual Monadic Scalors. The atlas is divided into forty sections (sublists) corresponding to the forty Genera of Form. In each section, the predicted absolute and relative degrees of analogousness between a single Genus and the other thirty-nine Genera is scaled, in order of descending overall analogousness. The possible range of analogousness values is 64 points, or from a maximal analogousness value of 64 (corresponding, for example, to the Genus's self-analogousness) to a minimal analogousness value of 0. These numbers represent the sum number of times the two (former) antimonads were judged to BOTH be either analogous or nonanalogous to the 32 former (directly scaled) scalees (here serving as virtual monadic scalors); the number of opportunities was 2 x 32, or 64, because of the duplication in the LEFT and RIGHT sets.
